Subject: Notice of third-party infringement claim & requested next steps

Hi Sean,

We received a takedown notice from a rights holder alleging that functionality in the Redwood-hosted integration used by Acme Payments infringes their IP. I'm attaching the vendor's claim notice and the alleged evidence (claim_notice.pdf).

Per Section 7 of the MSA we have with Redwood, Acme is giving you prompt notice and requesting confirmation of Redwood's defense/indemnity obligations for third-party IP claims that relate to the service. Our procurement team is preparing an order form amendment but legal wanted us to get your position first:

- Will Redwood accept defense and indemnity for this claim under the existing MSA?
- If yes, will Redwood accept the vendor's proposed form of counsel, or do you require the right to select counsel?
- Please confirm the initial preservation/evidence steps we should follow while we assemble the customer-side artifacts.

Acme needs a short mutual action plan we can share internally (legal + ops) within 48 hours. Can you loop in legal and confirm a point of contact?

Thanks,

J. Lawson
Senior Counsel, Acme Payments
legal@acme-corp.com

Attachment: claim_notice.pdf

Thanks, Sean and J. — I've reviewed the notice briefly and sketched a defensive approach. High-level points first:

- Redwood's standard MSA provides customer indemnity for third-party IP claims that "arise out of" the service as delivered, subject to notice and cooperation. We typically offer to defend with counsel selected by Redwood, but we will consider defense control carveouts in high-value or strategic deals.
- For Order Form-specific redlines, we should aim for: (i) narrow scope tied to actual use of the Service; (ii) notice and cooperation obligations; (iii) Redwood retained right to select counsel, with customer approval limited to conflicts; (iv) obligation to mitigate including possible temporary workarounds or deprecation.

I will prepare: (A) a short redline file with suggested language for the Order Form (redline_orderform.docx); (B) a preservation checklist Acme can follow now.

Evidence needs: the vendor's notice (received), export of API / feature logs covering the alleged transaction windows, any customizations or third-party plugins Acme installed, and the full chain of communications with the claimant. Please upload to the encrypted SFTP or share via the link below. If you prefer, Acme can send via secure email.

Quick suggested language (draft snippet):
"Redwood shall indemnify, defend and hold harmless Customer from any third-party claim ... to the extent the claim arises solely from Redwood's Service as provided under this Agreement. Customer must provide prompt written notice and allow Redwood to assume defense with counsel of its choice; Customer may reasonably object to counsel on conflict grounds."

I will try to get the redline and checklist to you within 6 hours so we can meet the 48-hour ask.

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com

Kimberly — thanks for the quick read and the draft snippet. A few clarifying points from our side:

1) Acme's procurement prefers that customers retain some right to approve outside counsel if the matter could materially affect Acme's public-facing product. We can accept Redwood selecting counsel for routine matters, but ask for a short approval window (48 hours) for counsel appointment.
2) Acme will pull logs and the communications chain and upload to the secure folder by EOD.
3) Can Redwood confirm whether indemnity would cover settlement amounts and reasonable defense costs?

Also, our security team flagged that they need a contact to handle the evidence handoff; copying Marta from logistics (marta@brightdata.com) who runs our Secure Transfer for these matters.

J.,

From a commercial/risk perspective here's what I'd propose to keep the deal moving while protecting Redwood:

- Offer: Redwood will defend and indemnify for third-party IP claims that demonstrably arise from Redwood's Service as deployed to Acme. That indemnity includes reasonable defense costs and settlements expressly approved by Redwood.
- Counsel selection: Redwood to select defense counsel by default; Acme may object within 48 hours for conflict reasons or material reputational risk. If Acme objects, Redwood will consider a joint-counsel path or shared oversight for that matter.
- Cap/limit: because this is a high-dollar strategic account, propose a carveout in the Order Form: indemnity for IP claims up to $10M aggregate, subject to standard insurance/mitigation recoupments. (Open to negotiation.)
- Evidence routing: Rafael — can your ops team receive the SFTP upload and confirm once we have the log package?

I can commit to the commercial language above in an Order Form amendment draft; Kim, can you align the redline to reflect the cap language and counsel clause? If Acme uploads the evidence by EOD today we will prepare the internal defense assessment within 48 hours and share a mutual action plan.

Thanks —
Lauren Bishop
